what_happened.line: The Select Board found the On the Rocks bar violated two liquor license regulations, on occupancy and a fight in and outside the premises, by a 3-0 vote.
The board set a seven-day penalty, December 31 through January 6, with closing at 8 p.m. and a written remedial plan required from the licensee.
The board then renewed On the Rocks' all-alcohol, Common Victualler and jukebox licenses, each by a 2-1 vote.
The board ratified the recreation director and assistant town accountant appointments.
A building design committee charge, including a project cost cap, was debated without resolution and is to be revised.

why_it_matters: The licensing decisions show how the board weighs a finding of violations against renewal: the bar faces a short early closing but keeps its licenses.

The cost cap for the municipal building design committee bears on how much the town may borrow for the project, and on whether it stays within the town's debt and fiscal policies alongside other projects.
watch_next: The revised design committee charge, with a cost cap, which the board is to amend as the town manager's financial roadmap develops.
The seven-day early-closing penalty at On the Rocks, starting December 31, and the written remedial plan due from the licensee.

why_it_matters: A single rate means homes and businesses are taxed at the same rate per thousand dollars of value, so the classification vote bears on how the levy is shared in the tax bill.

The special town meeting warrant is what residents will be asked to vote on, and the board's plan to pass over town hall articles and the fire contract's funding from an existing reserve bear on what reaches that floor.
watch_next: December 7 community kickoff meeting for the old primary school landscape project.
The special town meeting next week, including the passed-over articles and the fire union contract.

budget_items.what_was_said: Article for renovating the TC Passios into a town hall and community center was before the town at the earlier figure.
Alternative article would fund design development of a new building from free cash.
Estimates received that afternoon raised renovation about thirty percent and priced a new build far higher, citing material costs.
The town earlier allocated money to study a new build cost.
Design and engineering is billed as a percentage of project cost, with about forty percent spent before the decision point.
Delaying a decision adds cost each year, based on a construction cost index.
The finance committee chair estimated average household cost increases over 30 years and said the debt policy limit would be exceeded.
A member computed per-square-foot costs for the two options.
A bid below assessed value was discussed; the board declined to sell.
Fire chief received two grants for emergency planning and firefighter safety equipment.
Unitil winter rate increase was approved, and the aggregation rate was cited as an alternative.
Town manager noted there is no appropriation for the building, which runs on tenant rent, and added users risk a deficit to be addressed in the FY23 budget.

what_happened.line: Most Select Board members said they favored passing over both TC Passios articles at the special town meeting, but took no formal vote.
New cost estimates arrived the afternoon of the meeting, raising the renovation estimate and pricing a new build far higher, with material costs cited.
The board voted down the sale of parcel 7 off Pratt Street, with three members opposed, and said it will not re-bid the parcel.
The board awarded the 30 School Street landscape architecture proposal 4-1 and put six articles on the consent calendar unanimously.
The marijuana host community agreement review was deferred until after the November 16 special town meeting.

why_it_matters: The TC Passios articles decide whether the town hall and community center project goes forward, and the debt that follows would be paid mostly through property taxes.

Residents at the special town meeting will be asked to vote on these articles after the committees heard the new cost numbers only hours before, so the figures and the board's positions are worth reading first.
watch_next: The design committee's recommendation on the TC Passios articles, due the Wednesday after this meeting.
The November 16 special town meeting, where the board will state its positions and residents vote on the articles.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-1 to put articles K and L, the TC Passios rehab and new-build design-funding items, on the special town meeting warrant, subject to amending L.
The board unanimously added article J, the TC Passios building design committee's report, to the warrant.
Members said on the record that if K fails and L passes, they would vote to expand the TC Passios committee's charge.
The board approved signing the renewal of a bond anticipation note for the Saliva property and the ladder truck.
Discussion of demolishing the old primary school was tabled a week; the town manager is to ask whether the APDC chair's position against a pavilion is official.

why_it_matters: Articles K and L would ask voters at the November 16 special town meeting to fund design work on the TC Passios building, a debt-financed project whose borrowing a resident said could strain the town's debt capacity alongside Turkey Hill.
The design-documents funding, discussed as needing a transfer from stabilization or reserve, with free cash also raised as a source, would draw on town savings rather than a new tax line.
watch_next: The November 16 special town meeting vote on articles J, K and L, including the amendment to L.
Next week's Select Board return to the old primary school demolition, after the town manager asks the APDC chair about its pavilion position.

what_happened.line: The Select Board split evenly on whether to send the TC Passios renovation and new-build articles to a special town meeting, took no vote, and put the item on the Oct 5 agenda.
The board heard from the TC Passios design committee about three possible articles: a status update, renovation construction funding, and design funding for a new build.
Members objected to a draft demolition delay bylaw change that would add a daily fine; the article waits for town counsel's review.
The board voted to close Memorial Drive on Oct 23 for the Shrieks and Creeks event, with one abstention.
The board authorized the town manager to advertise parcel 7 as part of the disposition of 671 West Street.

why_it_matters: The TC Passios articles would ask voters for renovation construction money or new-build design money, so the timing of the special town meeting decides when residents are asked to vote on a large capital cost.

The assessors' proposed change to the elderly exemption would go to town meeting, and it is partly reimbursed through the state's cherry sheet in a variable amount, so the net effect falls on the tax bill.
watch_next: The Oct 5 Select Board meeting, where the TC Passios articles return to the agenda and the design committee is invited.
The Oct 28 joint Finance Committee and School Committee meeting on Chapter 70.

Members and the DPW director discussed who bears long-term road damage and whether a higher-standard road could be funded; Chapter 90 and pavement management funds were said to be insufficient.
The developer offered to grant the town a 10-foot-wide right-of-way strip at no cost.
A contractor mowed roadsides at a cost to the town; the DPW director plans to request similar equipment in the capital plan.
The town applied for a risk management grant through its insurance carrier to move to Microsoft Office 365.
The town plans to apply for a Community Compact IT grant for equipment upgrades, due October first.
The council on aging applied for a community enrichment grant to make the outdoor recreation area ADA compliant.
The assessors propose a special town meeting article raising the elderly exemption limit.
Accounts payable, deductions and payroll warrants dated August 31 were read, along with a voided payroll.

what_happened.line: The Select Board heard a preliminary presentation on a large warehouse at 475 Leominster-Shirley Road; no vote was taken and it goes next to planning board site plan review.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved a new three-year town manager contract, running July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2024.
The contract terms include a payout of unused vacation days, longer severance, deferred compensation, a higher phone allowance and three years of raises.
The board renewed six earth removal permits through August 2022, and held a change to Proctor's permit hours for a week after an abutter objected.
The town manager reported that the 30 School Street landscape architect RFP drew no proposals; it will return to a future agenda, likely with a changed timeline.
The board heard a cannabis retailer on its host community agreement and left the date of a community outreach meeting to the town manager.

why_it_matters: The town manager contract sets pay and severance terms for the town's top administrator for three years, which the town budget (mostly taxes) carries.
The unfilled 30 School Street design RFP means that project is delayed, and any new timeline or fee could come back as a budget request.
The cannabis host community agreement and the earth removal permits affect neighbors directly, and abutters can still comment before the Proctor vote.
watch_next: Aug 24, 2021: the Select Board's vote on the Proctor earth removal permit hours change, and the opening of the warrant for a special town meeting set for Nov 16, 2021.
The conservation boundary survey estimate, due on next week's agenda.

what_happened.line: The Select Board put off a decision on the pay-as-you-throw bag fee increase and a senior bag relief pilot until next week, to take public input first.
The board voted unanimously to rescind the pandemic-era vote letting the chair or vice chair sign warrants alone on the board's behalf.
The board ratified two seasonal lifeguard appointments, all in favor.
Members thought the draft RFP for old primary school landscape architecture is too broad for the town meeting appropriation and may need phasing; feedback goes to the town manager.
The board heard about a MassHousing site approval request under Chapter 40B for Pond View Commons, then moved to executive session on the town manager contract.

why_it_matters: The bag fee is a per-household cost: the board is weighing a smaller increase paid from surplus against a larger one, and a member said that surplus will be used up, so a further increase next year is likely.
The old primary school RFP sets how far the town's design money can go, so a broad scope could mean the work is phased across more than one appropriation vote.
watch_next: The board's next-week agenda: the bag fee, the senior relief pilot, and a vote on board goals.
The finalized old primary school landscape architecture RFP, which the board aims to complete next week.

No recorded votes were taken; the next meeting was set for Tuesday May 18th on Zoom, then June 1st.

watch_next: Tuesday May 18th on Zoom, then June 1st, are the next Select Board meetings.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to recommend the revised prior-year expense article, the revised capital plan article with changed funding sources, and the revised omnibus budget.
A motion to recommend Article 26, the TCP design fees, failed for lack of a second, and the board deferred its position until after the Article 25 presentation at Town Meeting.
The finance director gave the third-quarter FY21 report: local receipts ahead of estimate, interest income below it, no reserve fund draw, and a health insurance surplus expected.
The trash bid came in above estimate, so additional operating funds are covered by shifting capital funding sources.
The board appointed Karen Kemp to the Board of Registrars and will interview a second Republican nominee next week.

why_it_matters: The revised budget and capital articles are what residents will be asked to vote on at Saturday's Town Meeting, and the board's recommendations on them are now on the record.
Article 26 goes to Town Meeting without a Select Board recommendation, and a resident objected during public comment that no public hearing was held on the money.
watch_next: Town Meeting on Saturday, where the Article 25 presentation comes before the board gives its position on Article 26.
The board's interview of the second Republican registrar nominee next week.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to recommend most May 1 town meeting warrant articles, including the budget, capital plan and stabilization deposits.
Several articles (4, 18-19, 26, 30, 31) were deferred to town meeting rather than given a recommendation.
After a long discussion of its language, the board recommended Article 24, the APDC override, as amended, with one abstention.
The board heard the FY2020 audit, which had an unmodified opinion and no new management letter comments, and the auditor suggested reviewing old ambulance receivables for write-off.
The board signed the annual town meeting warrant for May 1, 2021 and the town election warrant, and voted to revoke the fuel storage licenses at 416 Electric Ave.

why_it_matters: These recommendations shape the budget, capital plan and override question that voters will be asked to decide at the May 1, 2021 town meeting.
The audit and the discussion of free cash and stabilization show how much the town holds in reserve, which bears on how much of next year's spending falls on the tax bill.
watch_next: Annual town meeting on May 1, 2021, where the recommended articles, including the amended Article 24, come to a vote.
The deferred articles (4, 18-19, 26, 30, 31) and the road ownership and utility digging question sent to town counsel for a future agenda.

Near the end it voted recommendations on articles with known amounts and held off on those lacking numbers.

Town deposit follows financial policy of 10 percent of prior year's certified free cash; sewer commission deposit is a consistent amount.
Small separate area billed for water bought from Fitchburg; usual operating amount stated.

what_happened.line: The board spent a long, divided stretch on the appointment and reappointment procedure and closed it for the night without resolving it.
By consensus it moved step four of the appointment procedure to the first Friday in April and the application deadline to the second Thursday in May.
The board will not recommend articles that lack a stated sum, such as the budget, capital, transfers, solid waste and cable, until numbers are available.
It voted recommendations on routine articles, merged the two OPEB deposit articles into one, and deferred to town meeting on the off-street parking article.
The Salary Administration Plan article was referred to the personnel committee, which is to vote on removing the longevity pay piece before the 30th.

why_it_matters: Articles with no stated sum, including the budget, are not yet recommended, so residents will not see the board's position on them until it votes again, possibly on the 30th.
The agricultural preservation restriction and the OPEB and sewer reserve deposits are items on the warrant that residents will be asked to vote on at town meeting.
How volunteers on town boards are reappointed is still undecided, and any change would apply to residents who serve on commissions.
watch_next: March 30 meeting, when warrant articles are to be approved for printing and the board may take up articles that still lack numbers.
Personnel committee vote, due before the 30th, on removing the longevity pay piece from the Salary Administration Plan article.

what_happened.line: The Select Board put an architectural preservation district appeal article and an old primary school landscape design article on the town meeting warrant.
The board held its vote on the Bright Farms TIF agreement for a week while the town manager asks town counsel whether missing the job count is a material breach.
Acceptance of the Bright Farms land parcel was postponed until the TIF agreement is executed.
The board decided senior tax relief is not ready for annual town meeting; staff will gather data on senior homeowners and run scenarios.
The board ratified a Council on Aging van driver and approved a virtual outreach meeting for Greenleaf Botanicals, 4-0 with one member away.

why_it_matters: The warrant articles, including the landscape design amount still to be set, are what residents will be asked to vote on at town meeting.
Senior tax relief will not be on this year's warrant, and the Wakefield-style program discussed would shift its cost to other residential taxpayers, so any later proposal bears on tax bills.
The Bright Farms TIF turns on how counsel reads "material", which decides what happens if the project falls short of its job count.
watch_next: Town counsel's view on whether missing the job count is a material breach, and the board's deferred Bright Farms TIF vote, expected in a week.
The amount for the old primary school landscape design article and the final wording of the preservation district article.
